steps.step: Add the firm tofu, carrot, bell pepper, and broccoli to the slow cooker.
Stir the red curry paste into the coconut milk and vegetable broth, then pour it over the vegetables.
Add the soy sauce and brown sugar and give everything a gentle stir.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are tender, about 4 hours — a slow cooker holds the coconut milk at a gentle heat so it stays silky instead of splitting.
Stir in the lime juice at the very end.
Scatter the thai basil over the top and serve over rice.
Press sauté on the pressure cooker, warm the vegetable oil, and brown the firm tofu for a few minutes.
Stir in the red curry paste and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, vegetable broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, carrot, and broccoli.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 3 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Stir in the bell pepper, which stays crisp in the residual heat, along with the lime juice.
Top with the thai basil and serve.
In a bowl, stir the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar, and the juice of one lime into a marinade.
Add the chicken thighs and marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for about 3 minutes.
Brush the chicken with a little vegetable oil and lay it in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry, flipping once, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, about 12 minutes — the rushing hot air crisps the edges without extra oil.
Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package, then rinse and drain.
Build bowls with the noodles, cucumber, and carrot, then the sliced chicken, lime, mint, and peanuts.
In a bowl, stir the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar, and the juice of one lime into a marinade.
Add the chicken thighs, coat well, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning once, until charred and cooked through to 165°F, about 10 minutes — the open flame adds a smoky char you cannot get in a skillet.
Meanwhile, cook the rice vermicelli according to the package, then rinse and drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls and top with the cucumber and carrot.
Slice the chicken over the top and finish with lime, mint, and peanuts.
Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch together in a small saucepan.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for about 3 minutes.
Lightly coat the chicken thighs with vegetable oil and lay them in the air fryer basket.
Air fry, flipping once, until cooked through to 165°F, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the sauce over medium heat until glossy and thick, about 3 minutes.
Brush the cooked chicken all over with the sauce, then slice it.
Serve over cooked rice, finished with the green onion and sesame seeds.
Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch together in a small saucepan.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Brush the chicken thighs with vegetable oil and grill, turning once, until cooked through to 165°F, about 10 minutes — the grill lends a smoky edge the stovetop version misses.
While the chicken grills, simmer the sauce over medium heat until glossy, about 3 minutes.
Brush the grilled chicken generously with the sauce.
Slice and serve over cooked rice with the green onion and sesame seeds.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Toss the carrot, zucchini, and mushrooms with the vegetable oil and spread them on the sheet pan.
Roast until tender and lightly browned, about 18 minutes, adding the bean sprouts for the last 3 minutes — roasting concentrates the vegetables instead of steaming them in a skillet.
Meanwhile, wilt the spinach in a dry skillet and toss it with the sesame oil, soy sauce, and garlic.
Stir the gochujang with a splash of water to make a spoonable sauce.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Divide the rice among bowls, arrange the roasted vegetables and spinach on top, and finish with an egg, the gochujang sauce, and sesame seeds.
Stir 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the juice of one lemon, the garlic, oregano, and a pinch of salt and pepper into a marinade.
Add the pork loin cubes and marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for about 3 minutes.
Spread the pork in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry, shaking once, until browned and cooked through to 145°F, about 10 minutes, then rest 3 minutes.
Stir the greek yogurt with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve over rice with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and the yogurt sauce.
Stir 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the juice of one lemon, the garlic, oregano, and a pinch of salt and pepper into a marinade.
Add the pork loin cubes, marinate for 15 minutes, then thread them onto skewers.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the skewers, turning, until charred and cooked through to 145°F, about 10 minutes, then rest 3 minutes — the grill is how souvlaki is traditionally cooked.
Stir the greek yogurt with the juice of the remaining lemon and a pinch of salt.
Serve the skewers over rice with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and the yogurt sauce.
Add the olive oil, onion, carrot, celery, chicken broth, and chicken breast to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is tender, about 5 hours.
Lift out the chicken breast, shred it, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook on high until tender, about 30 minutes — the rice goes in at the end so it does not turn to mush over the long cook.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice together, then whisk in a ladle of the hot broth to temper them.
Stir the egg mixture back in and let it warm through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with the dill.
Press sauté, warm the olive oil, and soften the onion, carrot, and celery, about 5 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, chicken breast, and rice.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Lift out the chicken breast, shred it with two forks, and stir it back in.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice together, then slowly whisk in a ladle of the hot broth to warm them.
Stir the egg mixture back into the pot on the residual heat — do not let it boil, or it will curdle.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with the dill.
Stir the greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, and cinnamon into a marinade.
Add the chicken thighs and marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for about 3 minutes.
Lay the chicken in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry, flipping once, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, about 12 minutes.
Rest, then slice and serve over rice with the tomato and cucumber.
Stir the greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, and cinnamon into a marinade.
Add the chicken thighs and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning once, until charred and cooked through to 165°F, about 12 minutes — the char echoes the crisp edges of a shawarma spit.
Rest the chicken a few minutes, then slice it into strips.
Serve over rice with the tomato and cucumber.
Combine the ground beef, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Shape into 8 small ovals and brush them with the olive oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F for about 3 minutes.
Arrange the kofta in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry, turning once, until browned and cooked through to 160°F, about 10 minutes.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, and serve alongside.
Combine the ground beef, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl.
Shape the mixture around skewers into long ovals and brush them with the olive oil.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the kofta, turning, until charred and cooked through to 160°F, about 10 minutes — the flame deepens the spices the way stovetop cooking cannot.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the kofta with the yogurt sauce.
Brown the andouille sausage and chicken thighs in the olive oil in a skillet, then transfer them to the slow cooker.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and cajun seasoning.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is tender, about 5 hours.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook on high until tender, about 45 minutes — adding the rice late keeps it from overcooking in the long braise.
Check the chicken reads 165°F and scatter the parsley over the top.
Press sauté on the pressure cooker, warm the olive oil, and brown the andouille sausage, about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken thighs, onion, bell pepper, and celery and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cajun seasoning until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the rice, diced tomatoes, and chicken broth, scraping the bottom well so nothing sticks and triggers a burn warning.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 5 minutes.
Fluff the jambalaya, check the chicken reads 165°F, and scatter the parsley over the top.
Brown the andouille sausage in the olive oil in a skillet, then transfer it to the slow cooker.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, red beans, cajun seasoning, bay leaf, and chicken broth.
Cover and cook on low until thick and the flavors have melded, about 6 hours.
Mash some of the red beans against the side of the cooker for a creamier pot.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and serve over rice.
Press sauté, warm the olive oil, and brown the andouille sausage, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cajun seasoning, then add the red beans, bay leaf, and chicken broth.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Mash some of the red beans for a creamier texture and remove the bay leaf.
Season with salt and pepper and serve over rice.
Blend the green onion, garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, brown sugar, lime juice, vegetable oil, and salt into a paste.
Coat the chicken thighs in the paste and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning often, until charred and cooked through to 165°F, about 14 minutes — an open grill is the authentic way to cook jerk, and the smoke is part of the flavor.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Blend the green onion, garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, brown sugar, lime juice, vegetable oil, and salt into a paste.
Coat the chicken thighs and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F.
Arrange the chicken on a foil-lined baking dish and roast for 25 minutes.
Switch on the broiler and broil the top for 3 to 4 minutes, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 165°F — the broiler mimics the grill's blistering finish.
Rest a few minutes before serving.
Stir the soy sauce, white vinegar, garlic, bay leaf, black pepper, brown sugar, and water together in the slow cooker.
Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat them in the sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is very tender, about 6 hours.
Lift the chicken out; for a thicker sauce, tip the liquid into a skillet and simmer to reduce, about 8 minutes — a slow cooker will not reduce liquid the way a stovetop braise does.
Remove the bay leaf and spoon the chicken and sauce over rice.
Press sauté, warm the vegetable oil, and brown the chicken thighs, about 5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, white vinegar, garlic, bay leaf, black pepper, brown sugar, and water.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Press sauté again and simmer the sauce until glossy and slightly thickened, about 6 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and serve the chicken and sauce over rice.
Brown the chicken thighs in the olive oil in a skillet, then transfer them to the slow cooker.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, turmeric, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chickpeas, and dried apricots.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is falling-apart tender, about 6 hours.
Check the chicken reads 165°F, then stir in the lemon juice.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Press sauté, warm the olive oil, and brown the chicken thighs, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chickpeas, and dried apricots.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 15 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Check the chicken reads 165°F and stir in the lemon juice.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Add the vegetable oil, onion, garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, garam masala, red lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth to the slow cooker.
Stir once to combine everything.
Cover and cook on low until the lentils are soft and the dal is thick, about 5 hours.
Stir well; if it looks thin, leave the lid off for the last 20 minutes to let it reduce.
Season with the salt and finish with the cilantro.
Press sauté, warm the vegetable oil, and cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the red lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 6 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes — a natural release keeps the lentils from spitting through the valve.
Stir well, season with the salt, and finish with the cilantro.
Add the olive oil, onion, carrot, garlic, white beans, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and rosemary to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are tender and the broth is rich, about 6 hours.
Mash some of the white beans against the side of the cooker for a thicker stew.
Stir in the kale and cook on high until wilted and tender, about 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Press sauté, warm the olive oil, and soften the onion and carrot, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the white beans, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and rosemary.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Mash some of the beans, then press sauté and stir in the kale until wilted, about 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Add the butter, onion, carrot, celery, chicken breast, and chicken broth to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is tender, about 5 hours.
Lift out the chicken breast, shred it, and return it to the pot; it should read 165°F.
Stir the flour, baking powder, a pinch of salt, and the milk into a thick, sticky dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the surface, cover, and cook on high until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through, about 40 minutes — keep the lid on so they steam rather than dry out.
Season with salt and pepper and scatter the parsley over the top.
Press sauté, melt the butter, and soften the onion, carrot, and celery, about 5 minutes.
Add the chicken breast and chicken broth.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Lift out the chicken, shred it, and return it; it should read 165°F.
Stir the flour, baking powder, a pinch of salt, and the milk into a sticky dough.
Press sauté, drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering broth, cover with a glass lid (not the pressure lid), and cook until the dumplings are set, about 12 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with the parsley.
Combine the ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, the minced half of the onion, garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper, then shape into 4 oval patties.
Brown the patties in the vegetable oil in a skillet, about 5 minutes, then set them in the slow cooker.
Scatter the sliced onion and mushrooms over and around the patties.
Whisk the flour and tomato paste into the beef broth and pour it over the top.
Cover and cook on low until the patties are cooked through to 160°F and the gravy has thickened, about 5 hours — the low, slow braise does the tenderizing a quick pan-sear cannot.
Season the gravy with salt and pepper and spoon it over the patties.
Prick the sweet potatoes all over and rub them with a little of the olive oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for about 3 minutes.
Air fry the sweet potatoes until tender all the way through, about 35 minutes, turning once — the air fryer gives the skins a nice chew the microwave cannot.
Meanwhile, stir together the black beans, corn, red onion, cumin, chili powder, the lime juice, and the salt.
Split each sweet potato and fluff the insides with a fork.
Fill with the black bean mixture, then top with avocado and cilantro.
Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork and set them on a microwave-safe plate.
Microwave on high until completely soft when squeezed, about 10 minutes, turning once — the microwave does in minutes what the oven does in the better part of an hour.
Meanwhile, stir together the black beans, corn, red onion, olive oil, cumin, chili powder, the lime juice, and the salt.
Split each sweet potato and fluff the insides with a fork.
Spoon the black bean mixture into each potato.
Top with the diced avocado and a scatter of cilantro.
Add the rice, vegetable broth, water, ginger, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge, about 7 hours — an overnight slow cook means you wake up to breakfast already made.
Stir well and season with the salt.
If it is thicker than you like, stir in a splash of hot water.
Ladle into bowls and top with the green onion and a drizzle of sesame oil.
Add the rice, vegetable broth, water, ginger, and garlic to the pressure cooker.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 25 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Stir hard — the grains break down into a silky congee as you stir.
Season with the salt and loosen with a splash of hot water if needed.
Ladle into bowls and top with the green onion and a drizzle of sesame oil.
Grease the inside of the slow cooker insert well.
Toss the peaches with 1/4 cup of the granulated sugar and the cinnamon, then spread them across the bottom.
Whisk the flour, the remaining granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract until just combined, then spoon the batter over the peaches.
Cover and cook on high until the topping is set and a toothpick comes out clean, about 2 hours — set a paper towel under the lid to catch condensation so the top does not turn wet.
Turn off the cooker and let it rest 15 minutes before scooping.
Melt the granulated sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat until deep amber, then pour it into a round baking dish and swirl to coat the bottom.
Whisk the eggs, sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and vanilla extract until smooth, then pour over the caramel.
Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Pour 1 cup of water into the pressure cooker, set the trivet inside, and lower the dish on top.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes — the gentle steam sets the custard without the fuss of an oven water bath.
Lift out the flan, cool, then refrigerate until fully chilled, at least 2 hours.
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate so the caramel runs down the sides.
Grease the inside of the slow cooker insert to keep the milk from scorching.
Add the rice, milk, granulated sugar, and salt and give it a stir.
Cover and cook on low, stirring once or twice, until the rice is soft and creamy, about 3 hours — stirring now and then keeps a skin from forming the way it would on the stove.
Stir in the cinnamon, vanilla extract, and raisins.
Let it sit 10 minutes to thicken; it firms up more as it cools.
Add the rice, milk, granulated sugar, and salt to the pressure cooker.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 12 minutes.
Stir well — it looks loose at first but thickens quickly as you stir.
Stir in the cinnamon, vanilla extract, and raisins.
Let it rest a few minutes to thicken before serving.
Rinse the sticky rice, then add it to the pressure cooker with 1 cup of water.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the coconut milk, granulated sugar, and salt in a saucepan just until the sugar dissolves — do not boil.
Pour most of the sweet coconut milk over the hot rice and let it soak in for 10 minutes.
Slice the ripe mango into thin pieces.
Plate the rice with the mango, drizzle with the remaining coconut milk, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Whisk the egg whites, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until frothy.
Stir in the shredded coconut until evenly moistened and sticky.
Preheat the air fryer to 320°F for 3 minutes and line the basket with parchment paper.
Scoop tablespoon-sized mounds onto the parchment, spacing them apart.
Air fry until the peaks and edges are golden, about 10 minutes — the compact heat toasts the coconut faster than a full oven, so watch the last minute or two.
Let the macaroons cool a few minutes to firm up before lifting them off.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then pat them very dry — the drier they are, the crispier they get.
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Preheat the air fryer to 390°F for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the basket in a single layer.
Air fry, shaking the basket every few minutes, until deep golden and crunchy, about 15 minutes — the air fryer crisps them faster than the oven, so shake often for even color.
Let them cool a few minutes, when they crisp up even more.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for about 3 minutes.
Air fry the corn, turning once, until charred in spots and tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic, and the lime juice.
Brush the hot corn all over with the creamy mixture.
Sprinkle with the cotija cheese and chili powder.
Finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the corn, turning often, until charred in spots and tender, about 10 minutes — the live fire is what makes elote taste like the street cart.
Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic, and the lime juice.
Brush the grilled corn all over with the creamy mixture.
Sprinkle with the cotija cheese and chili powder.
Finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for about 3 minutes.
Prick the eggplants, then air fry whole, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the insides are completely soft, about 25 minutes.
Let the eggplants cool, then scoop the flesh into a bowl and discard the skins.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and salt until creamy.
Spread onto a plate and drizzle with the olive oil.
Scatter the parsley over the top before serving.
Heat a grill to medium-high.
Grill the whole eggplants, turning often, until the skins are blackened and the insides collapse, about 20 minutes — charring over flame is what gives baba ganoush its signature smoke.
Let the eggplants cool, then scoop the soft flesh into a bowl and discard the skins.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and salt until creamy but still a little chunky.
Spread onto a plate and drizzle with the olive oil.
Scatter the parsley over the top before serving.
